the presence of fat in beef increased the heat resistance of Salm. typhilumurium DT104, but the presence of fat also resulted in longer lag phases.
Salm. typhi murium DT104 is more heat resistant in beef containing 18 and 24% fat than in leaner beef, as indicated by longer lag periods, longer D‐values and higher D‐log10 values.

the heat resistance of Salmonella typhi murium DT104 is influenced by temperature, fat level and the lag period.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal resistance of Salmonella typhi murium DT104 is significantly affected by fat content in beef.
